answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it may influence shared decisions. Votes are weighted by deposited value, and a challenge backed by evidence of duplicate control can trigger an audit; if Sybil identities are confirmed, their deposits are forfeited. This does not make identities impossible to fake, but makes influence costly: an attacker must tie up real capital for every extra identity and risk losing it. A ledge, a plume, or a cedar can be named in a challenge, but only verifiable evidence should justify slashing.
